premises.text: Many couples find therapy ineffective or poorly suited to everyday life and lack a digital relationship-health solution
premises.evidence_span: 11 to 18 percent of people that go to therapy find it to be not effective

premises.text: A metric-driven onboarding algorithm maps relationship vitals and delivers AI-guided check-ins and interventions
premises.evidence_span: through a proprietary algorithm, four key areas of the relationship have now been filled

premises.text: The platform complements therapy by holding between-session activities and progress visible to therapists
Go-to-market includes consumer acquisition plus partnerships with therapy-adjacent and employer assistance channels
premises.evidence_span: when it comes to the Employment Assistance Program

value.text: Relationship health tracked and improved in everyday life
value.evidence_span: LifeCouple is a Fitbit for your heart

causal_links.evidence_span: There is no digital solution. And now there is
This platform was built to keep a relationship healthy
13 billion dollars is lost of unproductivity because of people divorced or in an unhappy marriage

notes: Communication/trust/intimacy/conflict kept as facets of one vitals mechanism, not four premises. Icebreakers, digital gifts, and date prompts folded as intervention cascade. CAC/user metrics excluded as traction. Anti-template: need, product, and GTM separately revisable.
